editorial:
Imagine waking up after a violent robbery with a huge hole in your memory. That is exactly what happens to Korn. He is left trying to piece his life back together by writing everything down so he does not lose his thoughts. You can really feel his stress as he senses that someone else was involved in that crime, but he just cannot put a face to the name. The movie has a creepy, mysterious vibe that keeps you guessing if this is a psychological trip or if something supernatural is actually chasing him.

What really works here are the twists and the way the story builds up to that spooky 13th floor. The acting feels real, and the pacing keeps you on your toes. While some parts move a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you love a good ghost story mixed with a mystery, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the someone Korn was looking for was actually his own partner who died during the robbery. Korn had blocked it out because of the guilt. The ghost on the 13th floor was the spirit of his lost love trying to tell him the truth. Once Korn finally remembers the crime and accepts what happened, the ghost is able to find peace and leave him alone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural mysteries and twist endings.
